spans.text: Outside Galatea Sanatorium.
Frau Angelia!
Light catches up to Ange, panting heavily.
Boy.
Ange comes to an abrupt halt.
Hm?
If the situation were any different, I would never have let you follow me around.
If you insist on working with me, we've got to lay down some ground rules... First of all, don't "Frau" me.
Uh... Sure?
We'll leave the rest till later.
Ange turns away coldly and marches on.
(Sighs)
Don't mind her. Ange isn't being particularly hard on you.
She's like that to everyone.
Okay... Thanks.
Light smiles helplessly at AK-12 and gives her a nod before catching up with Ange again.
After a few paces, the grandiose building appears before them. Ange stops again, seemingly in no hurry.
So this is it? The sanatorium where Leone's been admitted to?
Yes, Leone is currently receiving treatment here.
Humph... I didn't think she'd agree to meet.
If she refused to see me, I wouldn't be able to force her in this kind of place.
Fortunately, Leone seems quite eager to talk.
She accepted your invitation almost immediately.
I hope she'll give us something useful.
Ange crosses her arms and glances at the main entrance.
For a place that's meant to be peaceful and quiet, there are a lot of random people hanging around, don't you think?
We're detecting a large amount of cameras.
Light seems to have realized something and scratches his head sheepishly.
They're from Berlin Television Broadcasting.
Berlin Television Broadcasting?
The main branch of the Deutscher Fernsehfunk, the largest state-sanctioned broadcasting company in Germany.
What are news reporters doing here? Other than Leone, are there any other high-profile patients in this sanatorium?
Maybe...it isn't a patient.
Ange gazes at the door thoughtfully.
In the sanatorium.
An interview with a certain high-profile figure is well under way in an isolated room.
Thank you very much for making the time to attend this interview today, Mrs. Gray.
You are very welcome. This is something we've agreed upon.
It is very important for someone like me to play nice with exceptional reporters like you.
You jest. As one of the best surgeons in Germany...in the entire world, even...
I doubt you'd need to pay any heed to public opinion.
Haha... I don't believe it is a reporter's job to sway public opinion.
Your remark makes it clear that you still harbor some kind of misunderstanding and skepticism towards me.
The way I see it, your job is to showcase the true side of society for more to see.
In a certain sense, you are the bridge through which we communicate with the people. It is entirely up to you to convey our aspirations accurately.
Does that mean you consider yourself separate from "the people", Mrs. Gray?
The young and attractive reporter asks a very pointed question, but this woman known as Mrs. Gray is not fazed at all.
Indeed. Many are afraid of admitting this⁠—a fear that I don't understand.
As a doctor, I have dedicated most of my life to spreading hope to more people.
This is precisely why I know better than anyone else that scalpels alone will not improve people's lives.
I wish to become an advocate who can bring about positive change and improve the welfare of the people.
To do that, I must first come to terms with what I'm doing.
If I don't even have the courage to admit it, why should people believe in me?
You sound exactly like a politician.
But I must say you are incredibly persuasive. If you ever decide to run for office, I will definitely vote for you.
Thank you, Miss Shadowless. You honor me with your support.
Now back to the subject. We wish to learn more about "Idunn", the new anti-Collapse serum that Galatea is about to distribute, in the interview today.
Idunn is being marketed as an affordable but highly effective drug. According to the spokesperson of your company, it is completely unlike any other existing drugs.
This bold claim has been called into question by multiple scientists and dignitaries, but as a surgeon, you are extremely outspoken in your support for Idunn.
Nobody doubts your professional skills or ethics, but it's quite interesting that you would vouch for Galatea's product even though you are in their employment.
Does your support stem from any commercial consideration?
I agree that to an outsider, it must be strange for a surgeon to vouch for an anti-Collapse formulation.
After all, certain medical fields are sometimes so far apart they might as well be different industries altogether.
People are having misgivings mostly because of this. How would you respond to such doubts?
Here's my response—don't worry, I will never exploit the trust that my patients have in me.
I may have a bit of a reputation, but I'm still only one among all my fellow physicians.
My confidence in Galatea's new product is based on its own merits. I simply wish more people will benefit from its success and receive better medical treatment.
Thanks to Galatea's prevalent marketing campaign, Idunn's alleged effects are no secret in Berlin.
The drug has indeed yielded some remarkable results in clinical trials, but it still has to go through a lot of standard procedures before official distribution can begin.
The general public perceives this vetting process as evidence that the government is impeding Idunn's distribution and is even taking to the streets in protest.
Is this a premeditated marketing strategy on Galatea's part?
<Size=30>...Hey, Shadow!</Size>
The recent unsanctioned demonstrations in Berlin are deeply regrettable.
Galatea gives the government its full support and understanding in following standard procedures. We also have absolute confidence in passing the rigorous vetting process.
Please wait patiently for dawn to break.
Do not fall before the first ray of sunlight pierces the darkness.
Thank you once again for attending this interview.
Shadowless closes her notebook and bows politely to Gray.
I'm sorry that the interview had to be cut short.
No problem at all. I understand you have an extremely busy schedule that's frequently subjected to last-minute changes.
I am a bit curious though—why have you suddenly made a detour to this sanatorium? Do you have patients here?
No, this visit is not work-related; it's a personal matter.
I see.
In that case, we'll be taking our leave. The interview will air after some editing.
Thank you, Miss Shadowless.
Don't mention it. Just doing my job... Hm?
Shadowless suddenly lets out a sound of surprise while she is packing her bag.
Is something wrong?
No... It's nothing. I just saw a familiar face.
Sorry, Herr Wechsler, please tidy up for me. I'll be right back.
Hold on, Shadow!
Shadowless leaves the room in a rush.
Then if you'd please.
Dear me... Young people are always so driven.
If she caused any offense with her youthful candor, please do forgive her.
Not at all. Miss Shadowless is a brilliant young lady.
Mrs. Gray gets up from her chair languidly.
Excuse me while I go to the restroom.
The running faucet under which Mrs. Gray is washing her hands produces the only sound in the otherwise quiet restroom.
Mrs. Gray fastidiously cleans her long, slender fingers with foamy soap and rinses it under the faucet.
I don't take unscheduled interviews.
After pulling out several tissues, she starts tidying up her appearance in front of the mirror and says out of the blue.
In an inconspicuous corner of the mirror, a woman suddenly emerges.
Your reputation precedes you, "Lady of Ashes".
Please, just call me Gray.
Mrs. Gray dries her hands and inspects them again. Satisfied that they are thoroughly clean, she balls up the tissues and discards them in the nearby garbage can.
You don't seem at all concerned about being stalked by a stranger.
If you were a stranger, I would have alerted the guards immediately.
But I do have the patience to entertain a certain Miss Anna Viktorovna Tsoi.
You know me?
You are quite the big name in the Berlin government right now.
Should I be surprised that a doctor knows all about the government?
A lot of my patients gossip.
Ange gazes at the reflection of Mrs. Gray's serene face in the mirror and softly closes the restroom door.
I have some questions for you.
As a fellow woman, don't you understand the importance of respecting a lady's moment of privacy?
Through the mirror, Mrs. Gray sees what Ange just did, but it doesn't seem to alarm her. Instead, she casually takes out her pressed powder.
I don't have the need to preen in front of a mirror in a restroom.
With that face, I can see why you don't.
You've heard of Leone Michel, I gather?
Of course. Leone is an expert in biochemistry.
Galatea has offered an olive branch to her many times, which she repeatedly refused.
She is certainly a woman of character—just like you, Miss Angelia.
Her character didn't do her any good.
Hard to say if yours will also lead you down the same fate.
Ange's eyes narrow at Mrs. Gray's subtle threat.
There seems to be more to your relationship with her than you're letting on.
Sorry to disappoint, but I am both mentally and physically a heterosexual female.
Otherwise, you would make a decent partner.
Mrs. Gray puts away her powder and fishes out a lipstick. She turns around and looks at Ange.
Ange's gaze drift from the lipstick in Gray's hand up to her lips out of reflex as the flirtatious remark sinks in.
Gray seems to have no intention of applying the lipstick. She is just playing with it, twisting the lipstick piston up and down.
At her mocking and disdainful gesture, Ange inhales through gritted teeth and balls up her fists.
You know exactly why I've brought up Leone.
She couldn't have committed those crimes in Bremen all by herself.
She has somebody behind her, who pulled some strings to have her transported to Berlin—to this very facility—after she was arrested.
They also helped her evade legal sanctions.
What a gruesome tale.
So let me get this straight... You suspect someone exploited their authority to help Leone escape her punishment.
Then you appear before me under such pretext.
How astonishing. What on earth have I done to raise your unfounded suspicion?
The Flora Institute has a very limited number of collaborators, especially in Berlin.
The only person on that list who also happens to be here is you, Mrs. Gray.
After twisting her lipstick up and down countless times, Gray finally lifts it up to her lips and applies it delicately.
Ange watches her go through the practiced motion. Her lips, painted bright red to begin with, appear even more sultry.
Is that all you've got?
I don't even know what to say... Don't you think you've made quite a few logical leaps in your deduction process?
The Angelia I've heard so much about is an extraordinary special agent.
Not some third-rate detective who makes groundless accusations based on subjective speculations.
Gray replaces the cap on her lipstick and smacks her lips lightly with hooded eyes.
Ange is still watching her unblinkingly, gauging her reaction.
You've worked together. That's evidence enough for me.
A surgeon collaborating frequently with Leone, who specializes in biochemistry.
What were the two of you doing?
Gray lifts her head and stares at Ange coldly. She slowly reaches into the right pocket of her coat.
Ange is bracing herself for whatever Gray extracts from her pocket, but it turns out to be nothing but a lollipop.
Miss Angelia.
If I remember correctly...you're from the Soviet Statesec, aren't you?
From my limited understanding, there has been some conflict between you and Statesec, and you do not answer to them anymore.
Yet here you are, all alone in Germany, being in frequent contact with the Stasi.
If everything I just stated is true, I must admit you have me very much intrigued.
What exactly are you doing here? What happened between you and the Neo-Soviets?
...Humph.
Gray shoves the wrapping she just removed into her pocket and puts the lollipop into her mouth, leaving only the stick hanging outside.
Everyone has their secrets, Miss Angelia. I understand if you do not wish to satisfy my curiosity.
After all, who doesn't have a skeleton in their closet?
My situation is also rather complicated. Trade secrets are still secrets, even if they aren't anywhere near as important as state secrets.
Every word she just said sounds like jab at Ange.
Your non-answer is an answer in itself.
This whole business lacks a logical explanation.
And since you refuse to give me one, I'm afraid I'll have to substitute it with my own.
Gray's lollipop stick wiggles up and down like the pendulum of her thoughts.
After a moment of silence, she shrugs and opens her mouth hesitantly.
Actually, I answered this very question just a few minutes ago...asked by a reporter.
The research of the Flora Institute is indeed rather irrelevant to my profession, but I have never been one to be constrained by such field categorizations.
I simply wish to make this world a better place—I know you may find that hard to believe, but it is the truth.
I have both the interest and courage in trying new things as long as I see the potential.

This goes for Leone's work as well as Idunn. I have also funded a lot of other research. If you're so inclined, you may investigate them one by one and I'll be happy to assist in your investigation. After all, I don't know if there are other cases like Leone in my portfolio.
She lets out a sigh. The lollipop knocks against her teeth inside her mouth.
Leone is very talented. Her research could have been such a boon for humankind.
I deeply regret that she has gone down this misguided path.
She was used.
The real source of evil is whoever's manipulated her from behind the scenes.
Then I sincerely wish you all the success in hunting down this manipulator and bringing them to justice.
Ange's fingers twitch.
It suddenly occurs to her that she is dealing with someone who's a different kind of trouble.
What if the people who interviewed you finds out about this scandal?
Then I'll be forced to issue an apology.
I will apologize for not discovering my collaborator's criminal intent in time and denounce the Flora Institute for their unethical practices.
Meanwhile, the Gray Institute of Biotechnology will make a donation to support medical aid.
After that, this incident will be swept under the carpet, along with anyone who investigated it?
You Soviet agents are so amusing.
Don't make a movie villain out of me, Miss Angelia.
I really do like you, you know.
...Do you now? Well, I don't know what I've done to deserve your admiration.
Perhaps one day, we will find ourselves standing on the same side, fighting for the same goal.
Before that, I don't mind making friends with someone like you—I don't usually bother wasting so much time on idle chit-chat with people I don't like.
Gray straightens up and makes for the door. She puts her hand on the door knob.
Ange grabs her by the arm out of reflex.
Gray's arm is incredibly slender. Ange has the feeling that she could snap this important tool upon which Gray's entirely livelihood depends if she just applied a bit more strength.
Other than wiggling her lollipop stick, Gray does not react to Ange's impudent action.
She gazes at Ange's arm and after a two-second pause, she reaches into her pocket.
Your prosthetic limbs seem to be in terrible condition, Miss Angelia.
You are very welcome to visit me at my private clinic.
I'd be happy to fix you up, free of charge.
She produces a name card and offers it to Ange.
On the card is her name, "Mrs. Gray", and the address of her clinic.
Ange slowly releases her grip and takes the name card wordlessly.
Are you this friendly to everyone?
Not at all. You're a special case, Miss Angelia.
Am I? I wonder why.
Gray takes the lollipop out of her mouth with an ambiguous half-smile and tosses it into the garbage can by the door.
She suddenly leans in close to Ange, who takes a step back instinctively, only to find a wall directly behind her.
It's been a pleasure talking to you, Angelia.
...Tell me, do you miss the time you spent in Bremen?
Gray's lips hover right next to Ange's earlobe. She murmurs each word distinctly in a low, husky voice.
While Ange is still frozen in shock, Gray has already opened the restroom door and swanned off.
Wait!
Ange recovers from her momentary daze and bursts through the door in pursuit.
Gray is already on the other end of the hallway with two security guards in tow.
Just before she disappears around the corner, she glances back at Ange with a sly smile.
Flipping hell... Dammit!
Ange punches the wall in anger. Sprinkles of dust fall from the ceiling.
The toilet in a locked cubicle inside the restroom suddenly flushes. The door opens and RPK-16 saunters out.
What an interesting woman, don't you think?
It's her.
She's the one behind Leone! There's no mistake!
What a shame. Maybe I should've made my move before she left?
...There's no point. We can't do anything to her.
She knows that, which is why she was being so brazen.
Should we just take her out?
That's even more pointless. Paradeus surely has more than one Gray.
I understand.
Ange inhales deeply to collect herself.
Gray's face is deeply imprinted into her mind.
This isn't over yet... Just you wait.
